scope: Selected 2014–2017 events; later legal outcomes retained. First release, not an exhaustive dossier.
methods: Read selected Mueller Volume I sections and Cohen criminal information text
Visually inspected House email PDF page 3
Read Flynn statement of offense and checked later pardon
Compared official case outcomes, appointment record, UN outcome and presidential proclamation
Read both congressional release notices and contemporaneous White House response

fec.title: FEC MUR 6961: campaign response, background section
fec.kind: Campaign legal response filed with FEC
fec.limit: A party submission; establishes the campaign’s stated announcement and filing dates, not an FEC finding on other allegations.

explore.title: March 18, 2015 campaign exploratory announcement
explore.limit: Campaign-authored statement preserved by Democracy in Action.

nh.title: New Hampshire visits, 2013–2014
nh.locator: April 12, 2014 Donald Trump / Freedom Summit entry
nh.limit: Event context, not a formal candidacy filing.

mueller.title: Mueller report, Volume I
mueller.locator: Printed pp. 1–2, 67–71; page numbers are report pagination, not viewer count
mueller.limit: Selected sections reviewed. Findings and declination language must stay together; underlying exhibits are distinct records.

cohen.title: United States v. Cohen, 18-cr-850: criminal information
cohen.kind: Filed charging document underlying guilty plea
cohen.limit: Read with the plea/sentencing record. Describes Cohen’s false statements; not a conviction of Trump.

cohenoutcome.title: DOJ Special Counsel case archive: Cohen entry
cohenoutcome.limit: The Moscow false-statements sentence is distinct from Cohen’s other criminal case.

trumpresponse.title: Trump’s November 29, 2018 remarks to reporters
trumpresponse.limit: Trump’s response and characterization, not an independent adjudication.

house.title: House release: three redacted Epstein email records
house.kind: Congressional publication of estate-produced email images
house.limit: Page 3 visually reviewed. Publication provenance is not independent authentication of every underlying assertion; no recipient bridge to Trump shown.

houserelease.title: Oversight Democrats’ November 12, 2025 release
houserelease.limit: Partisan characterization is attributed, not adopted as a factual finding.

housemajority.title: Oversight majority: additional Epstein estate documents
housemajority.limit: Release notice reviewed; the full estate production was not exhaustively reviewed for this series.

whresponse.title: White House response to the email release, reported by Reuters
whresponse.kind: Contemporaneous reporting of an official response
whresponse.limit: Secondary source for the White House response; not evidence resolving the emails.

israel2015.title: Trump postpones Israel visit, December 10, 2015
israel2015.kind: Contemporaneous news report quoting Trump and Netanyahu
israel2015.limit: Secondary reporting of public statements; no covert relationship established.

aipac.title: Trump’s March 21, 2016 AIPAC remarks
aipac.locator: UN Security Council / veto discussion and Jerusalem embassy pledge
aipac.limit: Evidence of what the candidate promised, not independent verification of all factual assertions in the speech.

flynn.title: United States v. Flynn: signed statement of offense
flynn.limit: Historical plea admission. Flynn later challenged the prosecution and received a full pardon; this is not presented as an outstanding conviction.

un.title: UN record of Security Council Resolution 2334
un.kind: Official meeting coverage and resolution record
un.limit: Establishes resolution outcome, not motives for every government’s vote.

jerusalem.title: December 6, 2017 Jerusalem proclamation
jerusalem.limit: The proclamation is a policy act; actual embassy opening is a later event.

pardon.title: November 25, 2020 Flynn pardon announcement
pardon.kind: Official White House announcement and defense
pardon.limit: Confirms pardon and the administration’s position. Its partisan narrative is attributed, not independently adopted.

acosta.title: Acosta sworn in as Labor Secretary, April 28, 2017
acosta.kind: Official Department of Labor appointment record
acosta.limit: Confirms office and date; does not establish the reason he was selected.

opr.title: DOJ OPR statement on Epstein’s 2006–2008 investigation
opr.limit: Poor judgment and failure in victim treatment were found; professional misconduct was not found.

epsteincharge.title: SDNY announces Epstein sex-trafficking charges
epsteincharge.limit: Charges are accusations, not a trial verdict; does not identify Trump as a charged participant.

epsteincase.title: United States v. Epstein: case status
epsteincase.limit: Epstein died before the 2019 charges were tried.
